q-122737.name: Question 2
q-122737.problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=(x-y)^{2}?$
q-122737.worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-y)^{2}) \\  & =2(x-y) \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-y)^{2}) \\  & =-2(x-y)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =2(x-y)\,i-2(x-y)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have to sketch the vector field at the points $(2,1),$ $(1,2),$ and $(1,-1).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the expression for $∇f.$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(2,1) & =2\cdot (2-1)\,i-2\cdot (2-1)\,j=2\,i-2\,j \\ ∇f(1,2) & =2\cdot (1-2)\,i-2\cdot (1-2)\,j=-2\,i+2\,j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =2\cdot (1-(-1))\,i-2\cdot (1-(-1))\,j=4\,i-4\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we draw the vectors starting at the corresponding points and obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14129144/assets/96851fd456d3b9f0a6af941a255926f35e29bbe778ed05556af3f69145e38ef2.png)

q-122738.name: Question 3
q-122738.problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{(y-2x)^{2}}{2}?$
q-122738.worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{(y-2x)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =-2(y-2x) \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{(y-2x)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =y-2x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =-2(y-2x)\,i+(y-2x)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have to sketch the vector field at the points $(1,1),$ $(1,3),$ and $(-2,-3).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the expression for $∇f.$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(1,1) & =-2\cdot (1-2\cdot 1)\,i+(1-2\cdot 1)\,j=2\,i-j \\ ∇f(1,3) & =-2\cdot (3-2\cdot 1)\,i+(3-2\cdot 1)\,j=-2\,i+j \\ ∇f(-2,-3) & =-2\cdot (-3-2\cdot (-2))\,i+(-3-2\cdot (-2))\,j=-2\,i+j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we draw the vectors starting at the corresponding points and obtain the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14129144/assets/2595c11a1b30fee9d76028010d2c7e608250c0d48ce0191d7da2a5412af6a110.png)

q-122789.name: Question 4
q-122789.problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the gradient vector field of the function $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{3}-2{y}^{2}}{4}?$
q-122789.worked_solution:
The gradient vector field of a function $f$ is given by $∇f.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{3}-2{y}^{2}}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2} \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{x}^{3}-2{y}^{2}}{4}) \\  & =-y\end{aligned}
$$

So, the gradient vector field of $f(x,y)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2}\,i-y\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have to sketch the vector field at the points $(-2,2),$ $(2,-3),$ and $(2,1).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the expression for $∇f.$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(-2,2) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot (-2)^{2}\,i-2\,j=3\,i-2\,j \\ ∇f(2,-3) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {2}^{2}\,i-(-3)\,j=3\,i+3\,j \\ ∇f(2,1) & =\frac{3}{4}\cdot {2}^{2}\,i-\,j=3\,i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we draw the vectors starting at the corresponding points and obtain the following diagram:
